Subject: Order form redlines — indemnity & evidence ask

Marcus / Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — excited about moving forward. Our GC has a couple of non-standard asks in the MSA/order form redlines (attached). High level:

- We need clearer language around third-party IP claims for model outputs — GC wants Redwood to defend and indemnify for infringement resulting from Redwood-provided models when the output is used as-is by Ecoroof.
- They want a limited evidence bundle showing sources/controls for model training + SOC2/ISO mindset to rely on.
- If Redwood will not accept full defend, GC is asking for an escrow or insurance-trigger path for remediation costs.

Can you confirm Redwood's stance and what evidence you can provide (SOC2, model provenance checklist, sample prompt/result provenance)? Attached: Ecoroof_MSA_redlines_v1.pdf (proposed MSA redlines).

Thanks,

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Order form redlines — indemnity & evidence ask

Alice — appreciate the clear summary and the redlines. Quick response to each point, and next steps below.

1) Defence/Indemnity for third-party IP claims
- Redwood's standard position: we defend and indemnify customers for third-party claims alleging that the service as provided (i.e., model weights and runtime) infringes a third party's IP, provided the claim arises from use within the agreed scope. We do not cover claims arising solely from customer-provided prompts, data, or outputs that are modified/used outside the intended scope.

2) Evidence & security artifacts
- We can provide our SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), a security pack (high-level architecture, dataflow, retention), and an evidence checklist that outlines what we can reasonably provide if a claim arises (logs, model config, training provenance summary where applicable).

3) Escrow / insurance path
- If we can’t agree on full defend terms, we typically propose either: (a) a defend-with-preservation-of-rights approach with an insurance-offset clause, or (b) an escrow-trigger that releases funds/technical artifacts only if a verified claim meets the trigger thresholds.

Attached is a short proposal with options and suggested tradeoffs (redwood-indemnity-proposal.docx).

Next steps:
- Kimberly (cc’d) will propose specific redline language we can try in the MSA/order form.
- Can we schedule a 30-min legal sync tomorrow or Monday to walk through options? I’ve linked the HubSpot deal where GC redlines are uploaded: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/EC-2028-0427

I’ll defer to Kimberly on firm legal language, but wanted to get you the operational evidence commitments up front.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood-indemnity-proposal.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

Hi Alice — looping in some suggested redline language below to make the tradeoffs explicit. Marcus, I put the snippets in plain text for quick cut/paste back into their draft.

Proposed language snippets (high level):

1) Scope of Redwood Indemnity
"Redwood will defend and indemnify Customer against any third-party claim alleging that use of the Redwood Service, as provided by Redwood under this Agreement, infringes or misappropriates such third party's intellectual property rights, provided that Customer: (a) uses the Service in accordance with this Agreement; and (b) promptly notifies Redwood in writing of the claim and cooperates in the defense."

2) Defense control / counsel selection
"Redwood shall have the right to assume control of the defense with counsel of its choice, provided that Redwood may not settle any claim that imposes an obligation on Customer without Customer's prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. If Customer reasonably demonstrates that the claim primarily arises from Customer's data or instructions, Customer may elect to assume control of the defense provided it notifies Redwood promptly and secures counsel acceptable to Redwood reasonably."

3) Escrow / remediation threshold (optional fall-back)
"If the parties cannot agree on a monetary settlement or allocation, and Customer reasonably demonstrates material damages arising from an infringement claim attributable to the Service, the parties agree to engage an independent technical arbitrator (pre-approved counsel list) to determine remediation scope. If remediation costs exceed USD 250,000, an escrow or insurance-trigger mechanism will apply as set forth in Order Form Schedule X."

Evidence & docs we can provide:
- SOC 2 (redacted) / summary of recent external audits
- Security pack (arch diagram, data retention, encryption, KMS integrations)
- Evidence checklist (logs, deployment manifests, KV cache snapshots, request traces) — note: we cannot provide raw training datasets except where licensed or required by law; we can provide provenance summaries for curated/partner-trained models.

I can convert the above snippets into a tracked-change redline of the MSA if you send the latest clean copy (or tell me where in Drive it is).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
[Attachment: legal-redline-snippet.txt (text/plain)]

Marcus / Kimberly — thanks for the quickly drafted options. A few clarifications from our side (GC + procurement):

- The GC can accept defend-with-preservation-of-rights in principle but wants stronger guardrails on Redwood controlling defense when claim relates primarily to output that includes Ecoroof proprietary data (customer logs / sensor feeds). In those cases, they want to either co-control the response or have the right to assume the defense.
- The USD 250k escrow trigger is workable as a negotiation starting point, but GC would prefer a lower threshold for consumer-impact incidents.
- Evidence: the SOC2 + security pack will help automatically — GC also asked whether Redwood can commit to preserving certain request logs and KV cache snapshots for a 12-month rolling period if that helps post-claim forensics.

We’re available for a legal sync Monday 9–11am PT or Tuesday 2–4pm PT. If you can confirm, we’ll get our GC and procurement on the invite.

Best,
Alice
